P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes, through NRB-licensed channels. Under NRB's Unified Foreign Exchange Circular 2082, foreign currency that card users earn online from service exports can be credited to their card (a prepaid foreign-currency card issued by a licensed bank). On request it can go to the person's own local-currency or foreign-currency bank account. The October 2026 amendment raised the threshold: card balances above USD 10,000 must be deposited into the cardholder's local or foreign-currency bank account (previous threshold not captured). Service exporters may spend from cards their foreign earnings plus USD 500 a year, capped at USD 10,000.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes, for qualifying FX earners. The circular provides for convertible foreign-currency accounts opened in the name of Nepali citizens, with specified permitted uses. For example, online FX earners may pay up to USD 25,000 a year for IT services related to their work through banking channels. Card balances from online service exports can be moved to the person's own foreign-currency account (P1). Note: some blogs claim individuals cannot hold FX accounts; the circular contradicts this for FX earners.

P3_local_gateways.question: Which local payment gateways can an individual or sole trader use to accept online payments?
P3_local_gateways.answer: Global platform availability for Nepal (automated collector snapshots, Oct 2026). Available: Paddle (not on its exclusion list; software sellers only, each seller reviewed); Whop (payouts); Dodo Payments (sellers); Google Play (developer registration); YouTube Partner Program. Not listed: Stripe (merchant sign-up); Lemon Squeezy payouts; Polar (payouts); Etsy seller payments.

P3_local_gateways.notes: Domestic wallets/gateways (Khalti, eSewa) onboard registered businesses. Khalti requires, for a sole or partnership firm, a Banjiya/Udhyog registration certificate, a PAN/VAT certificate, the latest tax clearance and proprietor ID, so an unregistered individual cannot become a Khalti merchant. eSewa merchant requirements not researched.

P4_paypal.question: Can residents receive money via PayPal?
P4_paypal.answer: No. A PayPal account can be created in Nepal (Nepal is a listed PayPal market), but Nepal is not on PayPal's receiving/Payouts list: no receiving of freelance payments and no withdrawal to Nepali banks. NRB has been exploring a PayPal tie-up via Fonepay since 2024–25, but no launch was announced as of 2026.

P5_payoneer_wise.question: Payoneer / Wise availability for residents
P5_payoneer_wise.answer: Wise: Nepal is NOT on Wise's list of countries whose residents can hold money. Payoneer: CONFLICTING. Nepali guides describe receiving into Payoneer and withdrawing to Nepali bank accounts, but an independent 2026 guide reports that Nepal support cannot be verified on any Payoneer-owned page and that withdrawal details trace to unofficial sources.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Freelancers not engaged in a business can work on a Personal PAN: the special 5% tax applies to resident individuals 'not engaged in business' (L3). Running a business needs firm registration (sole proprietorship 'Banjiya/Udhyog' registration) and a Business PAN. Separately, the E-Commerce Act 2081 (2025) requires anyone selling goods or services online, including via social media, to register on the Department of Commerce, Supplies and Consumer Protection (DoCSCP) portal. The penalty is up to Rs 200,000 per the Department; one firm cites up to NPR 500,000.

The Act targets e-commerce with consumers; Pioneer notes a micro/cottage-entrepreneur exception from the own-platform requirement. Act text and Gazette not read.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: The PAN (Permanent Account Number) from the Inland Revenue Department. There is no fee. For a Personal PAN an individual provides name, permanent address, father's name, date of birth and citizenship/ID number, with a copy of the citizenship certificate, a professional certificate copy and two photos. Converting to a Business PAN requires business registration.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Residents (normal abode in Nepal, or 183+ days in any 365-day period) are taxed on income from any source. Special regime: a resident individual NOT engaged in business who receives foreign-currency payment for software or similar electronic services provided outside Nepal (s.95क(6ख)), personal consulting services outside Nepal (6ग), or audiovisual content uploaded to social media (6घ) has 5% advance tax collected by the paying bank or money-transfer firm. Schedule 1 taxes such income at 5%. The rate was raised from 1% to 5% by Finance Act 2080.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is a single 13% rate (VAT Act 2052, s.7). Schedule 2 zero-rates services supplied to persons outside Nepal with no business presence in Nepal. Mandatory registration thresholds (set in the rules/Finance Acts) are about NPR 50 lakh annual turnover for goods and NPR 30 lakh for services or mixed businesses (secondary sources). Some professions must register regardless of turnover.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: The Individual Privacy Act 2075 (2018), supplemented by the Individual Privacy Regulation 2077 (2020). For corporate bodies and public authorities, collecting personal information requires competent-authority approval, the data subject's consent and notice to the data subject. Use or disclosure without consent is restricted except in listed cases. There is no dedicated data-protection authority.

sources.quote: Collection of Personal Information The Act requires fulfillment of the following criteria to collect personal information of natural persons: (a) approval of the “Competent Authority”, (b) consent of the data subject, and (c) information to the data subject.

L5_data_protection.notes: Official Act text (lawcommission.gov.np) not captured. Pioneer's scope note: the Act regulates data processed by public authorities or corporate entities incorporated under Nepali law; its application to individual sole traders is unclear.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: The E-Commerce Act 2081 (2025) requires e-commerce businesses to disclose name, address, contact, registration details, PAN/VAT and a grievance mechanism, and to list on the DoCSCP portal. Sellers must accept returns, cancellations or refunds for delayed, defective or misrepresented goods or services. No general no-reason cooling-off period was confirmed. The Consumer Protection Act 2075 also applies.

sources.quote: The Act requires E-commerce businesses, with the exception to micro-entrepreneurs and similar cottage entrepreneurs, to establish their own electronic platform, and clearly disclose business details (such as, name, address, contact details, and registration/regulatory approval-related information of the business, PAN/VAT number, grievance mechanism etc.)

L6_consumer_ecommerce.notes: A '7-day' return window appears only in a sample store policy (Blanxer), not the Act; not claimed.

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: (1) 5% tax on foreign-currency income from software or electronic services, consulting, and social-media content for resident individuals not in business (L3). (2) A 50% reduction in income tax, until FY 2084/85, on foreign-currency income of persons exporting IT-based services such as BPO, software programming and cloud computing (Income Tax Act s.11). (3) Exported services are zero-rated for VAT (L4). (4) NRB card and FX-account facilities for online service exporters (P1/P2).

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. (5) Local official channel: Nepal Rastra Bank lets online service exporters receive earnings on a licensed bank's prepaid foreign-currency card, and on request move them to their own local or foreign-currency account (P1/P2). Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.

sources.quote: (६) नेपाली नागरिकहरूको नाममा खोलिएको कुनै पनि किसिमको परिवर्त्य विदेशी मुद्रा खाताबाट सम्बन्धित खातावाला र निजको परिवारका सदस्यहरूलाई देहाय बमोजिम आवश्यक पर्ने परिवर्त्य विदेशी मुद्रा खर्च गर्न सकिनेछ ... अनलाइनमार्फत विदेशी मुद्रा आय आर्जन गर्ने नेपाली नागरिकले यस्तो कार्यसँग सम्बन्धित सूचना प्रविधि सेवा खरिद गर्ने प्रयोजनको लागि वार्षिक अधिकतम अमेरिकी डलर २५,००० वा सो बराबरको अन्य विदेशी मुद्रा सम्म बैंकिङ्ग उपकरण मार्फत भुक्तानी गर्न सक्नेछन्।

W1_workarounds.notes: Built from the platforms' official country lists on the dates shown. Availability changes, so re-check the platform's page before signing up. The 'Avoid' guidance is editorial, not a quoted source.

open_questions: Payoneer availability for Nepal residents is conflicting (Nepali guides vs. no Payoneer-owned confirmation).
E-Commerce Act 2081 penalty: Rs 200,000 (Department, via Kathmandu Post) vs NPR 500,000 (one law firm); whether the listing duty covers services sold only to foreign clients.
Whether the 5% tax under Income Tax Act s.95क(6ख)/(6ग)/(6घ) is final (s.95क is not in the s.92 final-withholding list; Schedule 1 fixes 5%).
NRB amendment of Oct 2026 (USD 10,000 card threshold) read only via two news reports; the amending circular itself not opened.
VAT registration thresholds (NPR 50 lakh goods / 30 lakh services) from secondary sources only; Finance Act 2083 changes not checked.
Interplay of the 50% IT-export concession (s.11) with the 5% individual regime not established.
eSewa merchant requirements and National ID card role in KYC not researched.
